mainTopic: Does שחיטה count from beginning to end or only at the end (the פרה אדומה and קרבן פסח proofs), and must שחיטה be one clear cut (שחיטה מפורעת)?
overview: This amud continues the question of whether שחיטה counts only when it is finished. First, the גמרא shows why the משנה of the פרה אדומה gives no proof: that משנה only deals with cases where the פרה becomes פסול. Then רב אידי בר אבין brings a משנה about slaughtering a פסח during the festival while owning חמץ. He uses it to argue that שחיטה counts from the first cut to the last. אביי answers that the partly cut animal can still be redeemed for the value of a פסח, and a ברייתא shows that a convulsing animal still counts as alive. Next, רב rules that cutting in two or three places on the neck is kosher. שמואל and ריש לקיש disagree, because they require one clear cut (שחיטה מפורעת). רבי אלעזר challenges them from a משנה about two people slaughtering, and רבי ירמיה explains it as one knife held by two people. רבי אבא attacks this from the wording of a ברייתא, and רבי אבין begins to reword it; his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The חכמים disagree: two may slaughter one offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes citing the source. The view of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון appears without his name, but the חכמים hold that two people may slaughter one offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is his view that is quoted without his name. But the חכמים say: two people may slaughter one offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a source from the previous lines. It shows that the חכמים disagree with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and allow two people to slaughter one קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer had tied the משנה to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who holds that two people cannot slaughter one offering. Now we learn that the חכמים disagree. This matters because, according to the חכמים, the משנה could have taught a case of two slaughterers.

keyTerms.meaning: Quoted anonymously, without the author's name
The Sages (the majority view)
An offering (קרבן) that is slaughtered

phrases.english: is cited unattributed,
phrases.notes: This is still talking about רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון from the lines just before. His view shows up without his name.

phrases.english: but the Rabbis say:
two may slaughter one offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים שְׁנַיִם שׁוֹחֲטִים זֶבַח אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the citation of a source begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים hold that two people may slaughter one offering, against רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.title: Even so, the משנה could have taught one man with two cloths
steps.stepSummary: Even according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the משנה could have taught a case where one man slaughters while switching cloths, so that only the second cloth becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, let the משנה also draw a distinction in a case where one man slaughtered with two cloths. The first cloth does not become impure, and the last cloth becomes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. Even if two people cannot slaughter one offering, the משנה could still have taught a case that shows שחיטה counts only at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שחיטה counts only when it is finished, then a cloth worn at the start of the cut, and removed before the end, was never on the slaughterer at the moment of שחיטה. So only the second cloth should become טמא. The משנה did not teach this case, which makes the idea that 'שחיטה counts at the end' look weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it distinguish (teach a contrasting case)
A cloth or scarf worn on the head
Becomes impure (טמא)
First / last

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
let it also distinguish,
phrases.notes: "It" is the משנה about the פרה אדומה being discussed.

phrases.english: such as where one man slaughtered
with two cloths,
phrases.notes: He starts the cut wearing one cloth and switches to the other partway through.

phrases.english: where the first cloth does not become impure,
and the last cloth becomes impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן נָמֵי לִפְלוֹג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Even the answer that relied on רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון does not fully explain why the משנה left out such a case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה about the פרה אדומה, read as fitting the idea that שחיטה counts only at its end.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If שחיטה counts only at the end, the משנה should have taught the case of one man with two cloths, which works even for רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. It did not.

steps.title: The משנה only deals with a disqualified heifer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה only discusses cases where the פרה becomes פסול. It does not discuss cases of a valid פרה, so its silence proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה is speaking about cases where the פרה becomes disqualified. It is not speaking about a valid פרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה left out the two-cloth case: the משנה is only interested in cases where the פרה becomes פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two-cloth case is about who becomes טמא from a valid פרה. The משנה's topic is a different one: when the פרה is disqualified. So the missing case is not a problem, and this משנה cannot be used as a proof either way.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualification
The red heifer
Validity, being fit for use
It is speaking about / dealing with

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה of the פרה אדומה only deals with a פרה that becomes פסול. It does not deal with a valid one, so it gives no proof about when שחיטה counts.

phrases.english: Rather, with the disqualification of the heifer
it is dealing,
with its fit state it is not dealing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by narrowing what the משנה is about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the משנה would list every case of who becomes טמא from the פרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only lists cases where the פרה becomes פסול, so leaving out the two-cloth case proves nothing.

steps.title: רב אידי בר אבין brings a משנה about the פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין opens a new objection, quoting a משנה: if one slaughters during the festival for the sake of a פסח, he is exempt; if not for its sake, he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין raised an objection: and during the festival, if he slaughtered it for its own sake, he is exempt; if not for its own sake, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins. רב אידי בר אבין quotes a משנה about the קרבן פסח to set up his objection, which the גמרא develops in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה deals with slaughtering a קרבן while owning חמץ. During the festival, slaughtering an animal as a פסח brings no punishment, but slaughtering it for a different purpose does. The attack itself is not stated yet; this line lays down the source it will use.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival (here, the days of פסח)
For its own sake (as the offering it was meant to be)
Exempt / liable

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin raises an objection:
and during the festival, for its sake, he is exempt,
phrases.notes: This is from a משנה in פסחים about slaughtering while owning חמץ. "For its sake" means as a פסח.

phrases.english: not for its sake, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the פרה discussion ends, a new objection opens from a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that שחיטה counts only at its end.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The attack is still being built. This line only quotes the משנה, and the next lines will draw the inference that creates the difficulty.

steps.title: The earlier inference: unspecified slaughter is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier discussion of that משנה: he is liable only because he slaughtered it not as a פסח, which implies that slaughtering with no stated intent would leave him exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: the reason he is liable is that he slaughtered it not for its sake. But if he slaughtered it with no stated intent, he would be exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalls an inference it once drew from this משנה. It is building toward רב אידי בר אבין's challenge, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only makes him liable when he clearly slaughtered for another purpose. From this we learn that slaughtering with no stated intent counts as slaughtering it as a פסח, which during the festival is פסול, so he is exempt. This inference is the building block for the coming objection.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (recalling an earlier analysis)
The reason is
But this implies (introduces an inference)
Unspecified, without stated intent

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read "for its sake" as a good thing here. During the festival, slaughtering the animal as a פסח (or with no stated intent) makes it פסול, and that is why he is exempt.

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
the reason is that it was not for its sake,
but with unspecified intent, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בָּהּ טַעְמָא דְּשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ הָא סְתָמָא פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה quoted in step 4 to build רב אידי בר אבין's objection.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the משנה we infer that slaughtering during the festival with unspecified intent leaves him exempt, because the animal still counts as a פסח and is therefore פסול.

steps.title: Why is he exempt if a פסח outside its time is a שלמים?
steps.stepSummary: The recalled discussion asks why a person who slaughters this פסח is exempt, since a פסח slaughtered at any other time of year is treated as a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is he exempt? A פסח during the rest of the year is a שלמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still recalling the earlier discussion and asks a question. If a פסח outside its proper time counts as a שלמים, someone who slaughters it with חמץ should be liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the case inferred in step 5: slaughtering with no stated intent (סתמא), which the inference says is exempt. But a פסח outside its day normally becomes a שלמים, and slaughtering a שלמים with חמץ during the festival makes a person liable. So why should unspecified slaughter be exempt?

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offering
The rest of the days of the year, meaning any time other than the proper פסח day

phrases.english: And why is he exempt?
phrases.notes: He means the person from the last step who slaughtered it during the festival with no stated intent, while owning חמץ.

phrases.english: A פסח during the rest of the days of the year
is a peace offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues recalling the earlier discussion of the משנה from step 5 and questions its exemption.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the משנה that slaughtering during the festival with no stated intent (סתמא) is exempt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסח outside its time automatically counts as a שלמים, and slaughtering a שלמים with חמץ makes a person liable. So the exemption seems wrong.

steps.title: A פסח outside its time needs its status uprooted
steps.stepSummary: The recalled discussion concludes that a פסח outside its time does not automatically become a שלמים. Its פסח status must be actively uprooted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: a פסח during the rest of the year needs its status uprooted.
steps.whatsHappening: The recalled discussion draws a conclusion from the question. A פסח outside its time stays a פסח unless someone actively uproots that status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה implies that slaughter with no stated intent is exempt, the animal must still count as a פסח, which is now פסול. It only becomes a שלמים through עקירה, meaning slaughtering it for the sake of something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Uprooting, actively removing the animal's פסח status
Conclude from it, a proven inference

phrases.english: Conclude from it:
a פסח during the rest of the days of the year
requires uprooting.
phrases.notes: Someone has to slaughter it for a different purpose. Otherwise it stays a פסח that is no longer valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 6 by drawing a new rule from the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A פסח outside its time stays a פסח that is פסול unless its status is actively uprooted.

steps.title: The rule applies only to owners pushed off to פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר גמדא reports that the חבורה limited this rule. Only when the owners were טמא מת and pushed off to פסח שני does the animal stay a פסח by default. Any other פסח becomes a שלמים without uprooting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר גמדא said: the group of scholars said that we are dealing with owners who were טמא from a dead body. They are pushed off to פסח שני, so the animal still stands for a פסח when no intent is stated. Only this kind needs uprooting. Any other פסח does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The recalled discussion narrows the conclusion. The משנה is talking about a special case: owners who were טמא and are now waiting for פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These owners still plan to use this animal on פסח שני, so slaughtering it with no stated intent is assumed to be for a פסח. That is why it needs עקירה. A regular leftover פסח has no future use as a פסח, so it becomes a שלמים by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to set the case up as a specific situation
Impure from contact with a dead body
The second פסח, a month later, for those who missed the first

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean every פסח outside its time needs uprooting. After this step, only the פסח of owners waiting for פסח שני stays a פסח by default. Every other one becomes a שלמים automatically.
steps.whyThisMatters: This special case is the setup that רב אידי בר אבין uses in the next step for his proof about how שחיטה works.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda said:
It was thrown out from the mouth of the group, and they said:
phrases.notes: Literally 'it was tossed out.' This idea came up from a group of scholars discussing the question.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
Such as where the owners were impure from a corpse,
who are pushed off to the second Pesach,
so that without stated intent, it stands for its own sake,
and it is this one that requires uprooting,
but another does not require uprooting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the conclusion of step 7 to one specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every פסח outside its time needs uprooting to become a שלמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the פסח of owners pushed off to פסח שני needs uprooting. Any other one becomes a שלמים automatically.

steps.title: רב אידי's proof: שחיטה must count from beginning to end
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין finishes his objection. If שחיטה only counts at the end, the first small cut would already push the animal out of being a פסח. The rest of the cut would then be done on a שלמים, and he should be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works if you say שחיטה counts from beginning to end, because then the animal became פסול from the very start of the cut. But if you say שחיטה counts only at the end, once he cut a little it was pushed off from being a פסח, and the rest of the cut is done on a שלמים!
steps.whatsHappening: Now רב אידי בר אבין uses the recalled case for his challenge. He argues that the משנה's exemption only makes sense if שחיטה counts from the first cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שחיטה counts from the beginning, the whole act happens while the animal is still a פסח that is פסול, so he is exempt. If שחיטה counts only at the end, the first cut already ruins it for פסח שני. Then it no longer stands as a פסח, and finishing the cut with no stated intent means slaughtering a שלמים, which should make him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: שחיטה counts from the first cut until the last
שחיטה counts only when the cut is finished
Was pushed off, rejected
A little bit

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
slaughter exists from beginning until end
it became disqualified from the beginning of the slaughter,
but if you say
slaughter exists only at the end
once he slaughtered a little of it,
it was pushed off from being a Pesach,
the rest, when he slaughters it,
it is a peace offering he slaughters!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the case set up in step 8 to finish the objection that רב אידי בר אבין began in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that שחיטה counts only at the end.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that view, the first partial cut ruins the animal for פסח שני, so the rest of the cut is done on a שלמים. Then he should be liable, which contradicts the משנה's exemption.

steps.title: אביי: it can still be redeemed for the value of a פסח
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that even if the first cut ruins the animal for פסח שני, it has not lost its link to the value of a פסח. It can still be redeemed and its money used for a פסח, so it still counts as a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: granted it was pushed off from being a פסח itself, but was it pushed off from the money value of a פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against רב אידי's proof. Even if שחיטה counts only at the end, the animal still has a פסח connection during the cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until the cut is finished, the animal could still be redeemed, and its money could buy a new animal for פסח שני. So it still stands as a פסח by default, and the exemption works even under the view that שחיטה counts only at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, even if we accept
The money value of a פסח, usable to buy a replacement

steps.whatToRemember: רב אידי בר אבין tried to prove from the פסח case that שחיטה counts from beginning to end. אביי deflects this: the animal still counts as a פסח through its money value, so the proof does not work.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
granted that it was pushed off from being a Pesach,
was it pushed off from the value of a Pesach?
phrases.notes: He means it could still be redeemed, and that money used to buy an animal for פסח שני.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: נְהִי דְּאִידְּחִי לֵיהּ מִפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אידי's objection in step 9 and defends the view that שחיטה counts only at the end.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the assumption behind the proof
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the animal is ruined for פסח שני, it no longer stands as a פסח at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It still stands as a פסח through its money value, so the exemption works even if שחיטה counts only at the end.

steps.title: A half-slaughtered animal can still be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא heads off an objection to אביי. Someone might say redemption needs the animal to stand before the כהן for valuation. A ברייתא shows that a convulsing animal still counts as fully alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that redemption needs the animal to be stood up and valued, didn't we learn: if one cut two סימנים or most of two, and it is still convulsing, it is like a living animal in every way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines someone attacking אביי's answer from step 10 and knocks that attack down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the partly-cut animal can still be redeemed for a פסח. Someone could object that redemption needs העמדה והערכה, and a slaughtered animal cannot stand. The ברייתא answers this: while it is still convulsing, it is treated as alive for everything, so it can still be stood up, valued and redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing the animal before the כהן and having him set its value, which is needed to redeem it
Convulsing, still twitching after being cut
Like a living animal in every respect

steps.whatToRemember: An animal that is still convulsing after its סימנים are cut counts as alive in every way. So אביי's answer stands: it can still be redeemed for a פסח.

phrases.english: And if you would say: it requires standing and valuation,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:11–12: an animal being redeemed is stood before the כהן, who sets its value.

phrases.english: but didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט בָּהּ שְׁנַיִם אוֹ רוֹב שְׁנַיִם
phrases.english: If one cut two in it, or most of two,
phrases.notes: 'Two' means the two סימנים, the windpipe and the food pipe.

phrases.english: and it is still convulsing,
it is like a living animal in all respects.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, בָּעֵי הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends אביי's answer in step 10 against a possible objection.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that a partly slaughtered animal can no longer be redeemed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The objection assumes the animal is already 'dead'. While it convulses it is still legally alive, so it can still be stood up and valued.

steps.title: Cutting in two or three places is a valid slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: if someone cuts in two or three different places on the neck, the שחיטה is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that רב said: one who slaughters in two or three places, his slaughter is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב gives a ruling: the cuts do not have to be in one single spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is someone who cuts a little in one place, then moves and cuts more somewhere else on the neck. רב holds that if all the cuts together reach the needed amount, the שחיטה works. The location does not have to be one continuous cut.

keyTerms.meaning: His slaughter is valid (kosher)
In two or three places on the neck

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
One who slaughters in two or three places,
his slaughter is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הַשּׁוֹחֵט בִּשְׁנַיִם וּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the פסח discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שחיטה done in two or three separate places on the neck is valid.

steps.title: שמואל requires a clear, single slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports that שמואל disagreed. He said שחיטה must be מפורעת, clear and obvious, and cuts in several places are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said this before שמואל, he said to me: we need a clear slaughter, and here there isn't one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה tells us שמואל's opposing view: the cutting in several places is not kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל adds a requirement that רב did not have: the שחיטה must be מפורעת, one clear and obvious cut. Cuts scattered over several spots fail this test, so for שמואל the שחיטה is invalid. This sets up a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: A clear, open, obvious slaughter in one place
And there isn't (any here)

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying the amount cut is too little. The amount may be enough. His problem is only that the cut is spread over several places and is not one clear cut.

phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel,
phrases.notes: 'I' is רב יהודה, telling us what happened when he repeated רב's ruling.

phrases.english: he said to me: We require a clear slaughter,
and there isn't one here.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אָמַר לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב's ruling in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחיטה must be מפורעת. Cuts in several places are invalid.

steps.title: ריש לקיש agrees and brings a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש also requires שחיטה מפורעת. He learns it from the פסוק in ירמיהו that compares a tongue to a 'שחוט' arrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש also holds that we need a clear slaughter. He said: from where do we know that slaughter must be clear? As it says: 'Their tongue is a sharpened arrow, it speaks deceit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that ריש לקיש holds like שמואל and gives the source in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the word שחוט for an arrow. That word comes from the same root as שחיטה. An arrow goes cleanly into one spot, so שחיטה must also be one clear cut in one place.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
A sharpened arrow; שָׁחוּט shares a root with שְׁחִיטָה

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ סָבַר:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish also holds:
we require a clear slaughter,
as Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
From where do we know that slaughter must be clear?
As it says: 'Their tongue is a sharpened arrow,'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 9:7. The word for 'sharpened' is the same word as slaughtering, and an arrow hits one clear spot.

phrases.english: 'it speaks deceit.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's view in step 13 with another אמורא and a פסוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 9:7, 'חץ שחוט לשונם', comparing שחיטה to an arrow.

steps.title: A משנה about two people slaughtering at different spots
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר challenges שמואל and ריש לקיש from a משנה. Two people slaughtering at different spots on the neck is kosher, even though it is not one clear cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר objected: if two people hold a knife and slaughter, even one above and one below, the slaughter is valid. Why? There is no clear slaughter here!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר attacks the rule of שחיטה מפורעת using a משנה that seems to allow cutting in two places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, one person cuts higher on the neck and the other cuts lower. That is two separate cut spots, just like רב's case. Yet the משנה says it is kosher, which seems to go against שמואל and ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Holding a knife
One higher up and one lower down on the neck
Why?

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar raised an objection:
Two people are holding a knife and slaughtering,
even one above and one below,
the slaughter is valid.
Why? But there is no clear slaughter!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שְׁנַיִם אוֹחֲזִין בְּסַכִּין וְשׁוֹחֲטִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the שחיטה מפורעת requirement from steps 13–14.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל and ריש לקיש's requirement of שחיטה מפורעת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה allows two people to cut at two separate spots on the neck. That is not one clear cut, yet it is kosher.

steps.title: The משנה means one knife held by two people
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers רבי אלעזר: the משנה about two people slaughtering is talking about two people holding a single knife together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to him: Our משנה is talking about one knife and two people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the challenge from the משנה. He says the two people in the משנה are both holding the same knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר thought the משנה meant two separate cuts in two places, which would go against שחיטה מפורעת. רבי ירמיה says no: there was one knife, so there was only one continuous, clear cut. So the משנה does not disagree with שמואל and ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the one just quoted)
One knife
Two people

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to him:
Our mishna is talking about one knife
and two people.
phrases.notes: Picture each person holding one end of the same knife, so there is just one cut.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: מִשְׁנָתֵינוּ בְּסַכִּין אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's קשיא against שמואל and ריש לקיש
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה describes two separate cuts in two places on the neck
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה describes one knife held by two people, so there is one clear cut

steps.title: The ברייתא's wording only fits two knives
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא challenges רבי ירמיה. The ברייתא on this משנה speaks of a worry that fits two knives, not one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to him: If so, does that fit what is taught about it, 'We are not concerned that perhaps they will make it טרפה because of each other'? If you say it means two knives and two people, that is fine. You might have thought we should worry that each one relies on the other, so neither one cuts the majority of the סימנים. So it teaches us that we are not concerned. But if you say it means one knife and two people, this line 'we are not concerned that perhaps they make it טרפה because of each other' should have said 'we are not concerned that perhaps they will press on each other.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא attacks רבי ירמיה's answer. He uses the exact words of a ברייתא that comments on this משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two knives, a real worry is that each person relies on the other, and neither cuts the majority (רוב) of the סימנים. The ברייתא's words fit that worry. With one knife pulled by two people, the natural worry would be pressing the knife down (דרסה), which makes a שחיטה invalid. Since the ברייתא does not mention pressing, it seems to be talking about two knives.

keyTerms.meaning: We are not concerned
They will make it invalid because of each other
They rely on each other
The majority (of the סימנים that must be cut)
They will press the knife down (דרסה), which makes a שחיטה invalid
It should have said

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבא is not arguing about the הלכה itself. His whole proof comes from which worry the ברייתא chose to mention.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to him:
If so, does that fit what is taught about it:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין שֶׁמָּא יִטְרְפוּ זֶה עַל זֶה?
phrases.english: 'We are not concerned that perhaps they will make it טרפה because of each other'?
It makes sense if you say

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁתֵּי סַכִּינִין וּשְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם – שַׁפִּיר,
phrases.english: two knives and two people; that works well,
because you might have said, let us be concerned
that perhaps they rely on each other,
and this one will not end up cutting the majority,
and that one will not end up cutting the majority,
phrases.notes: Majority of the סימנים, the windpipe and food pipe, which must be cut for a kosher שחיטה.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that we are not concerned.
But if you say
one knife and two people,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי ״אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין שֶׁמָּא יִטְרְפוּ זֶה עַל זֶה״ –
phrases.english: then this line, 'we are not concerned that perhaps they will make it טרפה because of each other',

phrases.aramaic: ״שֶׁמָּא יִדְרוֹסוּ זֶה עַל זֶה״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: should have said 'that perhaps they will press because of each other.'
phrases.notes: With two people pulling one knife in opposite directions, the knife could get pushed down instead of drawn across.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי ירמיה's reading of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's claim that the משנה means one knife and two people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's worry (each relies on the other, so neither cuts the majority) only fits two knives. For one knife, it would have mentioned pressing (דרסה).

steps.title: רבי אבין begins to fix the ברייתא's wording
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין answers רבי אבא by telling him to read the ברייתא differently. The new wording continues in the next line of the גמרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said to him: Read it this way: 'We are not concerned...'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין starts to defend רבי ירמיה by changing how the ברייתא is worded. This line sets up the next move; the rest of his new wording comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא's attack depended on the exact words of the ברייתא. So רבי אבין answers by saying we should learn the ברייתא with different wording, one that fits one knife held by two people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said to him: Read it this way:
'We are not concerned...'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אָבִין, תְּנִי: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's wording proves it is talking about two knives
steps.terutzMaskana: With the corrected wording, the ברייתא can fit one knife and two people
